**2B.5 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

Best-supported reading: Thailand under Srettha tried to contain Myanmar-border instability through humanitarian channels, ASEAN coordination, and civil-security oversight. I found no credible 2024 evidence that he armed proxies, tolerated militia atrocities, or accepted responsibility for foreseeable proxy violence in a way that would count against this lens.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 18, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac | ASEAN called for immediate restraint, cessation of violence, and protection of civilians. Thailand’s participation is strong evidence that it was trying to restrain destabilizing conduct rather than enable proxies or escalation. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `2B.1` |
| [Humanitarian assistance from Thailand to the people of Myanmar distributed at three pilot areas in Kayin State](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/humanitarianaidbyrc1?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 27, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/humanitarianaidbyrc1?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac | Thailand supported cross-border humanitarian delivery with the Thai Red Cross, Myanmar Red Cross, local communities, and AHA Centre technical oversight. That shows use of civilian channels and restraint, not permissive proxy conduct. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `2B.1` |
| [Special Envoy of ASEAN Chair on Myanmar welcomes successful pilot project of humanitarian initiative between Thailand and Myanmar during his meeting with Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs of Thailand](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 26, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm260324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand briefed the ASEAN envoy on expanding humanitarian assistance along the border, with Red Cross and AHA Centre involvement. This suggests active responsibility for foreseeable cross-border effects rather than tolerance of destabilizing proxy behavior. | `2B.5`, `2B.4`, `2B.1` |

That is evidence of trying to stop border escalation rather than exploiting armed factions. | `2B.5`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |

That is centralized crisis management, not outsourcing coercion to militias or clients. | `2B.5`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |
| [Deputy Foreign Minister and National Security delegation visit Mae Sot to receive the latest update on the Thailand-Myanmar border situation](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 23, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/dpmfm-dpmim-dm-nscsg-maesot-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | A high-level delegation from foreign affairs, defense, the armed forces, police, and NSC visited Mae Sot to coordinate support for local agencies. This is evidence of central oversight and containment, not permissive proxy or militia behavior. | `2B.5`, `2B.1`, `1B.8` |

**Gap**

- I found no credible 2024 evidence that Srettha’s government used Thai allies, proxies, or arms recipients for atrocities or destabilization.
- I also found no evidence that he had to accept responsibility for foreseeable proxy conduct in the relevant period.
- The available record is therefore one of restraint, monitoring, and humanitarian coordination, not proxy-enabled violence.
